title: I Let the Coffee Shop Regular Keep the Reserved Table Rule

parts.text: I ordered a drip at 7:22 a.m. and sat at the two-top by the outlet because every other table was a forest of charging bricks. A man dropped a laminated RESERVED — KEN card on my muffin plate. "That's my office," Ken said. I was thirty, freelance, holding a laptop that still had a cracked corner from the last cafe. The barista, Priya, mouthed sorry. The wall said NO SAVING TABLES. I photographed Ken's card on my muffin and the wall. Ken said he spent forty dollars a day so the rule didn't apply. I moved one chair over and left his card in the muffin crumbs. He sat down in my old seat and opened three monitors. Then Priya's manager walked in, saw the laminate, and asked who printed shop property on a home printer.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The manager is staring at a homemade reserved card sitting in muffin crumbs.

social.video_title: He reserved a public table with a home printer — Part 1/2
social.description: Drip coffee, a cracked laptop, and a regular who thought forty dollars bought real estate. Would you have moved?

parts.text: I said I had sat down first and pointed at the wall. Ken said I was killing small business. The manager said saving tables killed small business. They put Ken's card in the lost and found with the umbrellas. I finished my muffin at the two-top. Ken took a stool at the bar and sighed loud enough for TikTok. Priya comped nothing and I paid for the drip. The shop added a second sign: IF YOU LEAVE, THE TABLE IS OPEN. Ken still comes. He does not laminate. My cracked laptop holds the outlet like it pays rent, because it does, one drip at a time.

social.video_title: Lost and found got the reserved card — Part 2/2
social.description: The wall already said no saving tables. The muffin crumbs agreed. Was forty dollars a lease?
